PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid (uncultured)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Gestational Age: 17 weeks by ultrasound
Indication for Testing: Prenatal screening for chromosomal trisomies
Clinical Details: Routine prenatal screening

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniotic fluid cells using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. A minimum of four informative markers per chromosome were analyzed. Peak area ratios between 0.8-1.4 are considered normal (disomic), while ratios <0.65 or >1.8 indicate trisomy.

SAMPLE QUALITY
The amniotic fluid sample was noted to be blood-stained upon receipt.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13 markers:
D13S631: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D13S258: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D13S742: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D13S628: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable

Chromosome 18 markers:
D18S391: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D18S390: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D18S535: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D18S386: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable

Chromosome 21 markers:
D21S1411: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D21S1412: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D21S1435: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable
D21S1446: Multiple peaks detected - uninterpretable

INTERPRETATION
Two distinct genotypes have been detected at significant levels across all markers tested, consistent with maternal cell contamination (MCC). The presence of maternal cells in the amniotic fluid sample, likely due to blood contamination, precludes accurate determination of the fetal karyotype by QF-PCR.

The blood-stained nature of the sample significantly increases the risk of maternal cell contamination, as maternal blood cells can overwhelm the fetal cell population in the uncultured sample.

CONCLUSION
Results are UNINTERPRETABLE due to maternal cell contamination. QF-PCR analysis cannot reliably exclude or confirm trisomy 13, 18, or 21 in this sample.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. QF-PCR analysis will be repeated on cultured amniocytes, which typically eliminates maternal cell contamination as maternal cells do not grow in culture
2. A full report on cultured amniocytes will follow
3. If rapid results are clinically urgent, consider repeat amniocentesis with careful technique to avoid blood contamination

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
